topSignals.title: Elcogen crosses six weeks quiet (42 days) and Topsoe passes nine and a half weeks (67 days) — a full sweep across all three competitor tiers, the AI-datacenter deployment pipeline, regulation, competing on-site power, market/financials, research/IP, and the benchmark register again found nothing genuinely new.
topSignals.text: Direct English- and German-language searches for both priority stacks returned only standing background (factory/manufacturing history, the Aug 27 financial-outlook item already logged). A run-down of several apparently fresh-looking leads — an Oracle/Bloom "$251.6M warrant" item, a recirculating "Oracle swaps gas turbines for fuel cells" story, and two Chinese-broker SOFC/AI-datacenter research notes (Guosen Securities, Founder Securities) — confirmed all of them to be recycled April-September 2026 reporting, not new developments. Elcogen News | Topsoe press releases

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new news-archive item since Sept 21 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 42 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset, confirmed via English- and German-language searches today — 67 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by PTX/ammonia/SAF/blue-hydrogen news (a resurfaced "DKK 4.4bn PTX restructuring" item is the same Aug 27 release, not new), out of SOFC/SOEC scope.

Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation — round 4, completing this cycle's 8-company roster (Bloom Energy, Ceres Power): no new stack/cell-technology items for either; results were standing earnings/data-center-deal background and a recirculating Sept 2026 Oracle/Project Jupiter "delay rumor" story, already logged.
Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": no new item; results recycled standing background.

Today's Tier 3 dedicated rotation — cycle 6, round 2 (Watt Fuel Cell, OxEon Energy, Nexceris, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol), 7-day lookback: no new items for any of the six; OxEon's Oct 5 Mars-heritage SOEC/DOE-funding feature resurfaced again but remains the same already-logged item; the rest repeated standing background (Miura/Ceres 4.2 kW CHP launch, Nexceris $60M SOEC-scaling deal, Fraunhofer IKTS interconnect research).

Tier 3 sweeps — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant OR Weichai" and "Watt Fuel Cell OR OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura": no new item for either; results repeated the standing Sept 18 Doosan-Reverion $78M stack order/250 MW factory raise and the Miura/Ceres Japan launch. Chaozhou Three-Circle (CCTC) again returned no company-specific SOFC/SOEC news — continuing open data gap.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM, installation underway, hearing Dec 7), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B, Vineland NJ — first power block reported ready Oct 22; block capacity undisclosed; site not yet operational), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.
